name: Thyrocare Technologies Ltd
title: Thyrocare Technologies Ltd - 539871 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue up 24.3% to INR240 crores with EBITDA margin 32.2%; no capacity additions or capex cuts discussed, and specialty build-out is capex-light so far.

summary.headline: Thyrocare Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.3% YoY to INR240 crores, with EBITDA margin at 32.2% and PAT of INR51.3 crores (+34%).
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR240 crores (+24.3% YoY) and standalone revenue INR225.6 crores (+26.1% YoY), led by pathology growth of about 26%. Gross margin expanded more than 290 bps to 74.1% on better negotiations, 28% task volume growth and operating efficiency. EBITDA grew 34% to a 32.2% margin and PAT rose 34% to INR51.3 crores. Management formally launched specialty diagnostics commercially (allergy and genomics), announced plans to divest the nuclear imaging business, and restated test volumes to exclude calculated parameters.

financial_highlights.change: Management to use last four-quarter average

segments.name: Pathology - franchisee
segments.commentary: Franchisee business grew 27% YoY; active franchisees reached about 11,700, with 900 added in Q1. Value per franchisee has been around INR500 per month, and revenue per vial rose above INR250 from about INR240 per management's comparison.

segments.name: Pathology - partnership (B2B/B2C)
segments.commentary: Partnership business grew 26% YoY, led by insurance and health-tech partners and API integrations. Management said vial-level volume exceeds value growth due to discounting of incremental tests per patient.

segments.name: Aarogyam and Jaanch
segments.commentary: Flagship Aarogyam grew 21% YoY; Jaanch (curative, about 2% of pathology revenue) grew 36% YoY. Aarogyam is growing slower than non-Aarogyam tests, and Q1 is seasonally weak for preventive tests.

segments.name: Radiology
segments.commentary: Core revenue fell 4% YoY on centre consolidation but profitability improved. Management is pursuing divestment of the nuclear business; Q1 PAT for the radiology business was about INR1.72 crores, guided at about INR6 crores for FY27, against an investment of about INR140 crores.

segments.name: Tanzania (international)
segments.commentary: Revenue doubled YoY in the quarter, per management.

segments.name: Specialty diagnostics
segments.commentary: Commercial go-live in Q1 FY27 with allergy (Phadia platform) and genomics (NIPT, exome, NGS, gut microbiome, and others); over 20 specialised tests added. Specialty is under 1% of the test volume of about 5.5 crore tests.

guidance_outlook: Franchisee additions: management revised the expectation to about 500-700 per quarter. Q1 added about 900, with Q2 about 500, Q3 nil (seasonal), and Q4 about 500; some churn is possible, so not all 900 may remain by year-end.
Franchisee growth guidance held at mid-to-high teens for FY27; management said it would firm up guidance after H1.
Specialty diagnostics: ambition to reach 15-20% of portfolio (peer benchmark) in 3-5 years; no formal doctor coverage target set yet.
Specialty margins are expected to be broadly in line with current EBITDA margin unless volumes fail to materialise.
Radiology divestment: about 6 months process, no definitive buyer yet.
Consumables: announcement on Thyrocare-branded consumables expected by September.
No dividend guidance is given by management.
capex_capacity: Lab network at 43 labs in India plus 1 in Tanzania; three new labs opened in Q1 at Muzaffarpur (Bihar), Kurnool (Andhra Pradesh) and Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh).

Central processing labs in Mumbai and Delhi carry most specialty capex, which is already done; significant specialty capex is not expected in the next year beyond expansion capex if volumes exceed plan.
Phlebotomy network of about 2,000-2,100 phlebotomists; on-time arrival at 99%.
Over INR250 crores of capex invested over the period, per management.
demand_pricing: Franchisee revenue per vial rose about 7% YoY to above INR250, attributed to a mix shift away from thyroid (now low single-digit % of mix versus about 20% four years ago) toward lipid, biochemistry, multi-marker and PCR tests.
Partnership vial-level pricing shows erosion because incremental tests are discounted to encourage fuller panels; management said test-level pricing is broadly in line.
Franchisee network grew to about 11,700 active franchisees, a fourfold increase since the FY21 takeover. Field team roughly doubled over the year, from about 35-40 to about 70.
Channel strategy: pay-for-performance structure for franchisees, branded stores, and Madhuri Dixit as brand ambassador.
Specialty pricing: NIPT priced at less than half of competitors' prices; management aims for affordability and volume.

qa_highlights.question: How significant could genomics and allergy be in 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early for specific guidance; peers have specialty at 15-20% of portfolio, and management's ambition is the same level in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed for specialty in the next couple of years?
qa_highlights.answer: Most investment is done in the central Mumbai and Delhi labs; significant capex is not expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for imaging divestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Nuclear business has not grown or been invested in; process expected to take about 6 months, with no definitive buyer yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the test-volume definition changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Calculated parameters that are not billed were removed from test counts and past quarters restated; management said the variation is small.

qa_highlights.question: Will franchisee guidance be revised after 900 additions in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 500-700 per quarter is a reasonable run-rate, with Q3 nil; overall mid-to-high teens growth guidance held until H1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 900 franchisee addition sustainable and what is the Q1 PAT for radiology?
qa_highlights.answer: Adds reflect the enlarged sales team and branded stores; radiology Q1 PAT was about INR1.72 crores, with about INR6 crores expected for FY27.

risks_watch: Franchisee churn: management said not all 900 Q1 additions may remain by year-end, and the Q2 base is high (Q2 FY26 revenue about INR200 crores).

Parent-level debt: API Group debt reduced to about INR1,050 crores from INR1,700 crores; promoter holding is pledged. IPO or reverse merger is not planned and is at least 12 months away, per management.
Specialty execution risk: the segment is at a nascent stage, prescription-driven, and not yet scaled. Management has not set doctor coverage targets.
Aarogyam growth (21%) trails non-Aarogyam tests, so mix shift could dilute per-test realisation.
Consumables announcement expected by September 2026; details unknown.
Radiology divestment: no buyer identified; contribution is small (about INR6 crores PAT expected for FY27).
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and growth, with pathology up 26%, franchisees at a record and margins expanding. Cautious and evasive on forward guidance: management declined to revise franchisee or growth guidance until H1, and gave no specialty targets or dividend guidance.
key_quotes: I'm proud to say that after a strong growth of 20% in FY26, in Q1 FY27, our pathology business has grown even faster at 26%.
So, it's too early for me to revise guidance. I will still hold to the mid to high teens guidance at this point in time.
I think API will consider an IPO when it is profitable ex-Thyrocare, as well as debt free.
Test number is like-for-like and all numbers in the book are like to like.

adds.what: Three new labs opened in Q1 at Muzaffarpur (Bihar), Kurnool (Andhra Pradesh) and Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh)

growth.why: Franchisee growth guided at mid-to-high teens for FY27 (held), with a Q1 franchisee add of about 900 and a 500-700 per quarter expectation; Q1 pathology grew 26% and the franchisee base reached 11,700, but no revenue growth figure is guided for FY27 and no capacity beyond three newly opened labs is quantified.
